parts.label: (a)
parts.text: On Fig. 6.1, use the symbols + and - to indicate which of plates $X$ and $Y$ is the positive plate and which is the negative plate.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the electric field strength $E$ between the plates. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the electron.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Many electrons are now accelerated from rest from plate $X$ to plate $Y$ in Fig. 6.1. When the electrons hit plate $Y$, the absorption of their kinetic energies results in the emission of electromagnetic waves.
parts.text: Show that the minimum wavelength of these electromagnetic waves is $21\text{ pm}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the region of the electromagnetic spectrum that contains these waves.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain how these electromagnetic waves may be used to form images of internal body structures.

stem:
Two parallel metal plates $X$ and $Y$ are separated by a distance of $0.041\text{ m}$, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1.png}}

There is a vacuum between the plates. An electron is at rest at the centre of plate $X$.

A potential difference (p.d.) of $58\text{ kV}$ is applied across the plates. This causes the electron to accelerate towards plate $Y$.
